title: Budget All Spawned Script Commands
description: Extend the existing test-budget wall-clock timeout system in repo/lib/js/index.ts (runTestBudgeted, runCargoTestBudgeted) so that EVERY spawned command in the script.ts infrastructure has a hard wall-clock budget and gets SIGKILLed on timeout — not just cargo test/vitest/go test. Root cause: cargo check/build/clippy can hang 90+ minutes on the shared target/ dir lock when multiple sessions run concurrently, and today those calls go through unbudgeted runCmd (execFileSync, no timeout) or raw spawnSync, hanging agents forever. Add a default 10-minute Cmd budget to runCmd itself (via spawnSync timeout+killSignal), reuse the existing 20-minute Build budget for cargo build/clippy/check/wasm builds, keep the Test budget unchanged, and exempt dev servers/interactive apps/nx orchestrators explicitly. Rename the ⏱️TestBudget region to ⏱️Budget. Migrate call sites in repo/lib/js/index.ts, root script.ts, ui/tui/rs/script.ts, framework/renderer/wgpu/script.ts, framework/product/os/dev/script.ts, framework/core/script.ts. Add nx.json cache input for SEMIO_BUILD_BUDGET_MS on test targets. Extend repo/lib/js/index.test.ts with budget-kill tests.
summary:
Extended the existing test-budget wall-clock timeout system so every spawned command in script.ts infrastructure has a hard budget and gets killed on timeout, not just cargo test/vitest/go test.

Core (repo/lib/js/index.ts): renamed region ⏱️TestBudget → ⏱️Budget. runCmd now runs on spawnSync with a native timeout+SIGKILL instead of unbudgeted execFileSync; added runCmdStatus (returns exit status instead of throwing, for call sites that branch on it). Three budget classes: Test (unchanged, 15s/30s/5m/15m by level), Build (existing BUILD_BUDGET_MS=20min/SEMIO_BUILD_BUDGET_MS, now also the default for any `cargo` command via defaultBudgetMs()), and new Cmd (CMD_BUDGET_MS=10min/SEMIO_CMD_BUDGET_MS, the runCmd default for everything else). `budgetMs: null` exempts dev servers, interactive apps, and nx/script orchestrators whose own leaves are individually budgeted. Added budgetTimeoutHint() (cargo commands get the shared target-dir lock-contention hint) and buildBudgetMs()/cmdBudgetMs() resolvers. Unified message prefix to `[budget]`. runCargoLint and the three build spawnSync calls in runWasmPackWebBuild now carry the build budget.

Migrated call sites: root script.ts (classified ~15 nx run/run-many orchestrators and dev/mcp servers as budgetMs:null, cmake/ctest/vcpkg as build budget, os run as build budget unless --watch); ui/tui/rs/script.ts (cargo check ×2 → build budget); framework/renderer/wgpu/script.ts (cargo install/build/trunk build → build budget, trunk serve/cargo run native → exempt); framework/product/os/dev/script.ts (buildPlugin cargo build, engine wasm sub-builds, VerifyScript cargo test -p → build budget; cargo metadata got an inline timeout since it captures stdout; wgpu serve → exempt); framework/core/script.ts (typegen cargo test → build budget).

nx.json: added SEMIO_BUILD_BUDGET_MS as a cache input alongside SEMIO_TEST_BUDGET_MS on the four test* targets (it already affected their warm-build step).

Tests: added a "command budgets" describe block to repo/lib/js/index.test.ts (7 tests, ~1s) covering timeout-kills-and-throws, SEMIO_CMD_BUDGET_MS env override, budgetMs:null exemption, runCmdStatus, and budgetTimeoutHint selection — all pass in isolation (2 pre-existing unrelated failures in the same file, playground-host config, predate this change and are caused by concurrent in-progress work elsewhere in the repo).

Verified manually via sandboxed bun -e child processes (not touching the shared cargo target dir): a 250ms-budgeted 10s sleep is SIGKILLed in ~0.3-0.5s with the [budget] message and a throw; env override and budgetMs:null behave correctly; runCmdStatus returns the real exit code.

Known limitation (inherited from a pre-existing, already-documented Bun constraint, not introduced by this change): Bun's spawnSync does not honor `detached: true` to create a new process group, so runCmd's SIGKILL on timeout reaches only the direct child (e.g. cargo), not grandchildren (e.g. already-spawned rustc units). Killing the direct child still releases cargo's own target-dir lock — the actual reported 90-minute-hang cause — but an orphaned rustc unit can keep an stdio:"inherit" consumer's stdout pipe open until that one compile unit finishes on its own. Confirmed this in a live repo with heavy ambient concurrent cargo activity from other sessions; did not force-kill any process since ownership of orphaned PIDs can't be reliably distinguished from other concurrent sessions' legitimate work. True process-tree kill would require either a session/process-group wrapper (setsid-equivalent) or converting runCmd's ~50 call sites to the async tree-kill pattern runTestBudgeted already uses — noted as a follow-up, out of scope for this ticket.
